overview: Both are DNA vehicles used to carry a gene of interest into a host cell, but only one is built to actually make the gene's protein product.
genZNote: Cloning vector: just a delivery van, drops off the gene and leaves. Expression vector: the delivery van plus a fully staffed factory to actually produce the protein.

aspects.label: Main Purpose
aspects.valueA: Simply carries and replicates a gene of interest inside a host, for storage or amplification.
aspects.valueB: Carries the gene AND drives its transcription/translation into a functional protein.

aspects.label: Essential Elements Present
aspects.valueA: Origin of replication and a selectable marker.
aspects.valueB: Everything a cloning vector has, plus a promoter, ribosome-binding site, and other elements needed for gene expression.

aspects.label: Typical Use Case
aspects.valueA: Amplifying/storing a gene for later use, such as building a genomic library.
aspects.valueB: Producing a recombinant protein, such as insulin manufactured in bacteria.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Recombinant human insulin is made using an expression vector in E. coli — a landmark example frequently tested in biotechnology sections.
overlay.memoryTrick: Cloning vector = copy and store. Expression vector = copy AND cook (make the protein).
overlay.commonMisconception: Every expression vector is technically also a cloning vector — it just has extra features layered on top, not a totally separate category of molecule.
